• The user asks a simple question about a bug in a Python function. No tools needed — just answer directly.

  The bug: appending `&q=language:{language}` adds a second `q` parameter. GitHub's search API ignores duplicate `q` params (or uses only the first), so the language filter never applies. The fix would be to append the language qualifier to the `q` value itself (e.g., `q=created:>2023-01-01+language:python`), but they said don't rewrite — just identify.

  Also worth noting the URL encoding issue with `>` but the primary bug is the duplicate `q` param. Keep to 1-2 sentences.

• The bug is `url += f"&q=language:{language}"` — it appends a **second `q` query parameter** instead of adding the language qualifier to the existing search query. GitHub's API ignores the duplicate `q` param (it only honors the first one), so the language filter is silently dropped and results come back unfiltered; the language qualifier needs to be part of the single `q` value (e.g. `q=created:>2023-01-01+language:{language}`), not a separate parameter.
